extracted.intended_audience: military personnel, policy analysts, researchers, and others seeking Department of Defense doctrine, directives, and instructions
extracted.subtask_description: A reference/listing and explanatory guide to Department of Defense doctrine, joint publications, directives, instructions, manuals, and related policy documents relevant to intelligence and security. Includes definitions of doctrine, the purpose and function of directives and instructions, and the DoD subject-group numbering system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctrine is the fundamental principles by which the military forces or elements thereof guide their actions in support of national objectives. It is authoritative but requires judgment in application. (Joint Pub 1-02)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine is presented as authoritative guidance for military action, but users must apply judgment when implementing it; the citation to Joint Pub 1-02 anchors this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint publication hierarchy and keystone manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The joint publication hierarchy provides a framework for joint doctrine and joint tactics, techniques, and procedures. The organizational structure follows traditional joint staff lines of responsibility to the maximum degree possible. Each series provides for a keystone manual as the first publication in the series. The keystone manuals constitute the doctrinal foundation of the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the joint publication hierarchy as the organizing framework for doctrine and JTTPs; identify the keystone manual in a series as the primary doctrinal reference. The page also notes there are multiple online sources for joint doctrine and related publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of DoD issuances (Directives and Instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Defense (DoD) issues a large number of Directives and Instructions. The purpose of these issuances varies; however, all of them are used to internally manage the business of the DoD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat directives and instructions primarily as internal management instruments for DoD business across functions; recognize that specific issuances vary in purpose and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD Directives: scope and function
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD Directives are broad DoD policy documents containing what is required by legislation, the President, or the Secretary of Defense to initiate, govern, or regulate actions or conduct by the DoD Components within their specific areas of responsibilities. DoD Directives establish or describe policy, programs, and organizations; define missions; provide authority; and assign responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or using a DoD Directive, expect it to state required policy (often based on law or senior leadership direction), to define missions/organizations, and to assign authorities and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD Instructions: role in implementing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD Instructions implement the policy, or prescribes the manner or a specific plan or action for carrying out the policy, operating a program or activity, and assigning responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Instructions to find operational procedures, implementation details, and specific plans/actions that put DoD Directive policy into effect; Instructions are the implementing instruments rather than high-level policy statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD subject-group numbering scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The DoD Directives and Instructions are numbered according to the following eight major subject groups: 1000 - Manpower and Personnel (Civilian, Military, and Reserve); 2000 - International and Foreign Affairs; 3000 - Plans and Operations, Research and Development, Intelligence, and Computer Language; 4000 - Logistics, Natural Resources, and Environment; 5000 - Acquisition and Administrative Management, Organizational Charters, Security, and Public and Legislative Affairs; 6000 - Health; 7000 - Budget, Finance, Audits, and Information Control; 8000 - Information Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numbering groups to locate directives and instructions by subject area; the numeric prefix indicates major topical groupings and can guide search and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of doctrinal/policy materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The page organizes materials into categories such as JCS Joint Publications, Joint Chiefs of Staff Policy Documents, DOD Directives, DOD Instructions, Manuals, and 'Other' (various memoranda, DTMs, notes, and guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consulting DoD doctrine resources, identify which category a document belongs to (e.g., Joint Publication vs. DoD Directive vs. DoD Instruction) because the document type indicates its intended use, authority level, and typical content (doctrine, policy, implementation, or guidance). The page lists many individual publications with titles, dates, and incorporating-change notes as examples of each category.
